utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Judge Parker is withheld by other urgent matters this afternoon so Judge Thelin and I will sit alone. Good afternoon, Mr. Bushi. May I remind you of the affirmation you took yesterday which still applies today. So Mr. Mettraux will continue with the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Bushi.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You remember during your examination-in-chief the Prosecutor asked you a number of questions about Mr. Baki Halimi. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you explained that during the weekend of 10, 11, and 12th of August of 2001 you had a number of phone conversation with Mr. Halimi. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you said that Mr. Halimi was the person who was providing you information about what was going on in the village. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He informed me.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you have also said that, as far as you know, Mr. Halimi was not involved in your -- or in the activities of your organisation, the NLA. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. He was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But in fact, Mr. Baki Halimi is an NLA commander called, named or known as Commander Lisi and he is your man in the village, he is the man in charge of logistics and funds. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir, it is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can the witness please be shown Rule 65 ter 1D812.1, please. Your Honour, before we proceed any further into this document, we would like to indicate that this is a document which we have obtained from the security and counter-intelligence service of the Ministry of Interior. The redactions which have done into the documents have been done by us as a matter of precaution because of the source that is expressly mentioned in this document. We have the non-redacting copy of that document and what we would propose would be to tender both documents after we have gone through this particular document the redacted and non-redacted version, and we would propose that the non-redacted version be admitted under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, do you have that document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: As you can see from the top left-hand corner of that document this is a document that comes from the security and counterintelligence division, also known as the UBK part of the Ministry of Interior. It is dated the 22nd of August of 2001 and it relates to an interview that took place between 18 and 1930 on 12 August of 2001. And the line of work is political violence and terrorism. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the registry please turn to the next page of that document?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, I'll ask to you look for a paragraph which starts with the words: "Furthermore, he said that he heard ..." Can you locate that in the Macedonian version?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which paragraph is that?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I believe this would be the third paragraph in the Macedonian version. It starts with the word: "Furthermore, he said that he heard that prior to the events in the village of Ljuboten." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I read it out in the English version. It says this: "Furthermore he said that he heard that prior to the event in the village of Ljuboten Musliu had contacted someone from the self-styled NLA by telephone with the aim of involving the village in fighting. All of the aid, money, and food was carried by Halimi Bakim, father question mark Islam, born on 3 December 1953 in the village of Ljuboten, a teacher at the primary school in the village of Ljuboten. He also stated that he had heard that Lutfiu Ekrem, father, Lustim, born on 1 February 1965, in the village of Ljuboten was giving logistical report to the self-styled NLA, that is to say he was taking fighters into his home who had been fighting in the village of Tanusevci and Brest." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter couldn't hear the answer. Can you ask him please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, could you repeat your answer? The microphone didn't pick it up.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then it goes on to say: "To a direct question on the operatives who were behind the placement of the mine the source said that it was Xhavit Asani, however I do not know what they were planning up there, at Basinec pastures." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that information in this document, Mr. Bushi, it was accurate, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, could the witness then be shown what is Rule 65 ter 1D85, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, what I'm about to show you is a statement taken by the Office of the Prosecutor of Mr. Kenan Salievski. Do you recall that Mr. Salievski is a village leader in Ljuboten. Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you would agree that Mr. Salievski as a village leader would have a pretty good idea about what is happening in his village. Can you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'll ask the registry to turn to page 2 of that document, please. And if you could focus on paragraph 5 of this statement, please. Mr. Bushi, I will read the part of the statement of Mr. Salievski that he gave to the Office of the Prosecutor in November of 2004. He said this: "The only person who had real contacts with NLA was Baki Halimi, alias Commandant Lisi, from our village. Halimi was for a long time hiding his activities but I found out that he had contact with NLA. Saliu Naim, Rexhepi Supi, both from Ljuboten told me about Halimi's contacts with NLA because they were close to him." Sir, do you agree that Mr. Halimi was in fact involved with your activities from within the village of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not true. He was not involved at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can the registry please turn to page 9 of that same statement. That would be 1D00-1993. And I will ask the registry to focus on paragraph 41 of the statement, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, I will read another paragraph of the statement of Mr. Salievski to you. It says this: "Being asked what kind of support were Ljuboten villagers giving to NLA, I say that I do not know anything about this matter. You should ask Baki Halimi." Well, the Prosecution did that, and I will ask the registry to bring up what is Rule 65 ter 1D541. The Macedonian version would be 1D00-4956. Mr. Bushi, this is the -- another statement taken by the Office of the Prosecutor, this time of its own investigator, Mr. Thomas Kuehnel. Do you know Mr. Kuehnel?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe, if I see him. I can't say now.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, he was one of the investigator who was present during the signature of your statement in August of 2006. Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I have to look at him to tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, for the time being we'll look at his statement and I will ask the registry to turn to page 20 of Mr. Kuehnel's statement. That would be 1D00-4954. And in the Macedonian version that would be 1D00-4981, please. And if the registry could focus on paragraph 98, please. This is what Mr. Kuehnel said about this. He said this: "Upon the perusal of Macedonian government intelligence reports and upon receiving information from Ljuboten villagers and leaders, I learned about Baki Halimi or Halimi who allegedly had the title of Commander Lisi and who, in 2001, was and still is a village leader." And then he goes on to say: "Mr. Alimi informed me that he raised funds for the NLA during the period relevant to the indictment." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So, Mr. Bushi, is that your evidence that Mr. Alimi who was collecting funds for the NLA and whom you know and who was known in the village as Commander Lisi, you did not know that he was collecting funds and facilitating logistics for your organisation. Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would prefer to give a more lengthy answer, if Your Honour would permit me.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps, Mr. Bushi, if you answer my question first you can then add to it, if you feel like you should. Do you want me to repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The question is this: Is that your evidence that Mr. Alimi, who was collecting funds for the NLA and whom you know and who was known in the village as Commander Lisi, you did not know that he was collecting funds and facilitating logistics for your organisation. Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Baki Halimi was not a member of the NLA, never was engaged in collecting funds or providing logistical support. The people who were appointed to be engaged in raising funds had the authorisation of the General Staff or my own authorisation. Baki was not one of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So your evidence is that the UBK was wrong, Mr. Salievski was wrong, and in fact Mr. Alimi himself was wrong about his own role at that time. Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, such documents, beginning from the 14th of February, 2001, until September, all those documents provided by the intelligence and counter-intelligence service and the Ministry of Interior are unacceptable to us. As to what you put to me about his statement, then it is up to him to respond. I have no comment to make.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Bushi, you have addressed the issue of the UBK document, but then is that your evidence, that both Mr. Salievski, the village leader, and Mr. Alimi were not telling the truth to the Office of the Prosecutor, as far as you know and as far as can you tell?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what they said.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, we would seek to tender the document shown earlier to Mr. Bushi, which is Rule 65 ter 1D812 in the unredacted version and Rule 65 ter 1D812.1 in the redacted version. We'd ask that the first version be admitted under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: The Prosecution will object to this request. Not based on the authenticity of the document but based on the issue that this witness cannot speak about the content. Well, first he has only been shown a small part of the document, and secondly, he has not confirmed the information contained in the document. I'm sure that we had witnesses here who could have spoken about this document and we will have witnesses maybe from the Defense side or the Prosecution side who would be able to do that, but this witness so far has not corroborated the information contained in the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may respond very briefly that is very much the point of having the document tendered. The point is to show or to demonstrate the lack of credibility of this witness. The point is not to establish the truth of the content of the document through this witness. This witness has indicated he did not know of the document and does not trust its content. Our submission, Your Honour, is this document is relevant. The Prosecution has not taken issue with this. It is as my colleague has mentioned authentic. It is also relevant to the issue in this case, in particular as to the presence or not of the NLA in the village and more importantly, for the present matter about the credibility and reliability of the present witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may answer with regards to the credibility of this witness. First, another witness has to establish that this information is correct. And then we can go to the credibility or not of this witness, but so far this witness has established that this information is not correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: The exhibit will be received. It will be one exhibit with two extensions, one under seal and one not under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the unredacted version will Exhibit become 1D223.1 under seal, and the redacted version would become 1D223.2.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, do you recall yesterday that both my colleague and myself asked you in about the presence of members of your brigade in and around the village of Ljuboten. Do you recall being asked those questions?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall that I suggested to you that in fact the people, the members of your brigade who went to Ljuboten on the 12th of August had done so upon your order or authorisation, do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were no NLA members in Ljuboten, Your Honour. I'm repeating. If there were such soldiers in Ljuboten, the Macedonian forces wouldn't have been able to penetrate the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, what I'm putting to you, Mr. Bushi, is that a number of your associates or members of your brigade actually asked to you go to the village of Ljuboten. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He asked one person from Ramadan Limaj and we did not allow that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, what I'm putting to you is that at first you refused because you thought that the two special units, Teli's unit and Arusha's units, which were already in the area at the time, could take care of the security situation in Ljuboten. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And those two units, Mr. Bushi, were in the area because you had sent them there two days earlier to carry out the attack in Ljubotenski Bacila. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But when you realised that there would be problem extracting some of your men from the village you sent re-enforcements and allowed other members of your brigade to go to the village. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown Rule 65 ter 1D507. It has an ERN range 1D00-4667, and the Macedonian version would be 1D00-4674.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, I apologise there is no Albanian translation of this document. This is the statement of Mr. Suat Saliu. Do you agree that in July and August of 2001 Mr. Saliu was a member of the 114th Brigade, your brigade. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my recollection, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps then we can turn to page 2 of that document and focus on paragraph 2, please. Mr. Bushi, I'll ask to you look at paragraph 2 and I will read it out for you. It says this: "I joined NLA in June 2001 and initially served with the 113 Brigade. The 113rd Brigade was deployed in the area of Nikustak, Vistica, Matejce. I had a training session for about three weeks at the monastery at Matejce and then in mid-July, I joined the 114th Brigade. The commander of the 114th Brigade was Nazim Bushi. His deputy was Ramadan Limaj who arrived from Kosovo. He is the brother of another member of the Limaj family who is now in custody in The Hague." And if can you look at paragraph 3 of that same statement, the second sentence -- third sentence, I apologise. It says: "The 113 Brigade was operating in the area of Aracinovo, the 114th Brigade operated in the area of Skopje and Ljuboten and had two special groups, Teli and Arusha, Bear. The 114th Brigade was specifically formed to operate in Skopje area. It was formed after the Aracinovo battle." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If you could --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If the registry could please turn to the next page in the Macedonian version and go to the next page in the English version.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me. I would like to comment on paragraph 2 and 3, if I may. If I may, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Could you just answer the questions that are being asked ... [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: -- being asked --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Your statement you can make some additional --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't respond about paragraph 2 and 3. I said only I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That was not my question, Mr. Bushi.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There are untruths here.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, would you like to identify those then.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Ramadan Limaj was not my deputy. It was Halil Paloshi instead. And he -- Fatmir Limaj was not his brother, as it says here. They are simply from the same village, from Kosova. And in paragraph 3, it is written that Xhemail Jashari was commander of Brigade 113, which was not true. It was Sami Ukshini, aka Sokoli, the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But you agree --

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Brigade 113 until the formation of 114th Brigade operated. 114th Brigade is a continuation of brigade 113 and Aracinovo was the zone of responsibility of Brigade 114th.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But are you not taking issue Mr. Bushi, are you --

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: -- with the suggestion that he was indeed a member of your brigade, is that correct, you don't take issue with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't take issue with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If you could turn to paragraph 7 of the statement, please. It would be in the third page in the English and I believe the fourth page in the Macedonian. I apologise, the third page in the Macedonian as well, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, I would like to ask you to locate a sentence in paragraph 7 of this statement which would be somewhere in the middle of that statement and it starts with the word -- of that paragraph. It starts with the word: "After the mine incident had happened." Can you locate that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I will read it out for you. It says this: "After the mine incident had happened they all wanted to go down to Ljuboten to defend the village against the attack by Macedonian forces. On behalf of the group of fighters from Ljuboten, Islam Zendeli spoke about that with Bushi. Islam Zendeli lives in Ljuboten now. Bushi said that anyone who would take any action on his own initiative without orders would be arrested immediately. "He also said that Teli's group and Arusha would do the job of protection of Ljuboten. Islam Zendeli conveyed his message back to us. We calmed down and waited for an order. On Saturday morning, nothing happened, and as the shooting subsided, we thought that nothing would happen. At about 8.00 in the morning, my father called me and said that it was quiet. Fifteen minutes later, he called again and said that there was a lot of shelling and shooting and that boy Erxhan Aliu was killed." This would be in the next page in the Macedonian, please. Can you see that, Mr. Bushi?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree now that you had tasked Teli's group and Arusha to take care of the protection of the village of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't agree with that. I didn't send anyone there. Not Arusha nor Teli's group.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall that yesterday you told this Chamber that those two groups, Teli's groups and Arusha were two special units that were directly under your command. Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is true that they were directly under my command. I remember saying this, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you also recall to have said that the units and operations would not go without an order from you. Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So if indeed there was operation going on and that those two units were in the area at that time, that would have been as a result of an order of yours. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, then please turn to paragraph 8 of that same statement. That is still the statement of Mr. Suat Saliu. This is what he says: "At about 9.00 in the morning, all of us in the group of men from Ljuboten and the fighters from Teli's group received an order to leave from Nikustak. There were about 30 fighters in Teli's group. In Nikustak, we received ammunition. From Nikustak we continued our way to Ljuboten. Some volunteers joined us in Nikustak, in total we were about 70 fighters. On the way to Ljuboten, we joined with Arusha group at a place called H'iat e Ljubotenit [phoen] and continued for Basinec. There we split into three groups of approximately 20 fighters each. As we got closer to Basinec we split up into smaller groups." Can you see that, Mr. Bushi?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you would agree that this information is directly contradictory to what you have told this Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what Suat had stated. I can see the statement but what he is saying here is not true. I stand by what I said earlier, that I did not send anyone from 114th Brigade in Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, in that case we'll turn to tab 7 or, I apologise, this is Rule 65 ter 1D94. It is 1D00-1316. The Macedonian version would be 1D00-1322. Sir, what I'm about to show to you is an another OTP statement of Mr. Islam Zendeli and first I should ask you, do you recall that Mr. Suat Saliu mentioned in his own statement that Mr. Islam Zendeli had approached you and not Mr. Ramadan Limaj. Do you recall Mr. Saliu saying that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, if I can ask the registry to turn to page -- well, perhaps I will ask you this before. You are aware, aren't you, that Islam Zendeli was a member of your brigade. You know that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If I can ask the registry to turn to page 4 of the statement, please. That would be 1D00-1319 in the English and that would be 1D00-1325 in the Macedonian version. Sir, I will ask you to focus on paragraph 16 of that statement. And I should ask you that as an introduction as well. You knew that Mr. Zendeli was also a villager from Ljuboten, he was born in Ljuboten. Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Later I learned about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, this is what Islam Zendeli says: "When the attack took place my uncles called me from the village. During that night I had been guarding in Vistica and therefore woke up a bit later than usual. I think at around 7.00 or 8.00 a.m. My uncles told me that the village had been attacked and then we got information from soldiers who were together with me in Vistica. They told me that the village is under attack, the Macedonian forces are entering the village and doing massacres, raping women and so forth. At the moment we were shocked and decided with the other colleagues from Ljuboten to go to defend the village. My commander told me that, okay, since it is your village, you should go there to defend it." And the commander of Mr. Zendeli and the only one who could give order as you said for such operation, that was you, wasn't it, Mr. Bushi?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only me as far as orders to go to Ljuboten are concerned. Nobody else.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And as Mr. Saliu said and as was confirmed by Islam Zendeli, the discussion and the authorisation or approval to go to the area had come from you. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct. Here it says my commander. Which commander he is referring to, we had a battalion commander, squad commanders, platoon commanders, company commanders and the brigade commander which was me and I didn't have any contact with Islam Zendeli. Which commander is he referring to here? We had a platoon commander, as I said, a company commander, battalion commander and brigade commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well perhaps I can Help you identify the commander in question, Mr. Bushi, and I put it to you that it is you. If we can go back to Rule 65 ter 1D507 which is again the statement of Mr. Saliu. It would be 1D00-4670. Mr. Bushi, I will read to you a passage that I've have read to you a moment ago from the statement of Mr. Suat Saliu. It is taken from paragraph 7 of his statement. And he said this: "On behalf of the group of fighters from Ljuboten, Islam Zendeli spoke about that with Bushi. Islam Zendeli lives in Ljuboten now. Bushi said that anyone who would take any action on his own initiative without orders would be arrested immediately," and so on. So do you recall now that the commander to whom Mr. Zendeli Islam said he had spoken about this matter, the commander in question, that was you, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what Islam and Suat spoke about between themselves and who said what.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But the truth is, Mr. Bushi, isn't it, that Mr. Zendeli came to you to ask you for permission to go to the village. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct. As I said earlier, one person went to Ramadan Limaj, and I told Ramadan Limaj that nobody is allowed to go to Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, let's go on reading the statement of Mr. Zendeli Islam. This is Rule 65 ter 1D94. 1D00-1319, please. And in the Macedonian version that would be 1D00-1325. That would be page 4 of the Macedonian and page 4 of the English, please. Mr. Bushi, I'll ask you again to look at paragraph 16 of the statement of Mr. Zendeli and I will read out the rest of that paragraph to you. It says this: "Five of us left from Vistica and we decided to go to Nagustak where some other NLA soldiers joined us. These people were all not from Ljuboten but also from other locations. When we left Nagustak, we were some 30 to 40 people. In addition, some NLA soldiers from other locations joined us. Some of us were from the 114th Brigade but there probably were also member from some other brigades." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And again, Mr. Bushi, you will agree that the people whom Mr. Zendeli, Mr. Saliu and other joined were the members of Teli and Arusha's unit which you had sent earlier during that weekend.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'll ask you now to turn to paragraph 17 of this statement. I will simply read it out to you. We're going to come back to this issue in a moment. It says this: "We walked through the woods towards Ljuboten. It took us five to six hours to get close to Ljuboten. We got to the woods close to Ljuboten, in the area of Basinec, about 3 kilometres from Ljuboten village. The Macedonian forces noticed us and they started to shell at us. They were positioned in points, so we were attacked from Ljuboten side and from Rastak side. One of our soldier was killed. I know that he was from Nagustak. And five or six got wounded." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Now you recall that yesterday I asked you about a number of individual, Xhezair Shaqiri, aka Hoxha, Ramadan Limaj and Nazmi Sulejmani. Do you recall that I ask you about those?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you said that these three people were in or around Nikustak during the weekend 10, 11 and 12. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: In fact, again, that is not the truth, Mr. Bushi is it? Those three people were leading the operation in and around Ljuboten on your behalf. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown what is now Exhibit P215, please. This is N000-6475-N000-6493-01. And the Macedonian version would be N002-7240-N002-7256-01. Mr. Bushi, what I'm about to show you is --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps we should move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you. If I could ask the registry to turn to page 8 of the statement, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, I'll ask to you look at paragraph 33 of this statement, which is in front of you. This would be the next page in Macedonian as well.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. It is still not on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I think it starts on the previous page at the very bottom of the page. I apologise. In the Macedonian version. Thank you. Can you focus on paragraph 33, Mr. Bushi. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I will read it out to you. This is what (redacted) said in his statement. "The operation of the NLA on Sunday afternoon, 12 August, was organised and led by Xhezair Shaqiri." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that's the man who you claim was in fact in or around Nikustak at that time. Is that the same person?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is Xhezair Shaqiri.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then (redacted) said this: "He was responsible for strategic issues in the NLA. As I was told, Xhezair Shaqiri on this Sunday afternoon was with the soldiers above Pop Cesme. When the NLA soldiers were wounded, he ordered them to withdraw to Matejce because he was informed that the Ohrid agreement was reached and the war was going to end. After that, he left for Kosovo and I did not hear anything about him. Albanians respect him a lot. About 100 NLA members participated on Sunday afternoon operation in the area above Ljuboten." Can you see that, Mr. Bushi?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see all of it, but I heard the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, if the Macedonian version could be turned to the next page please -- or the Albanian version, thank you, to the next page. To the top of the page. Can you see at the top of the page that I just tried, Mr. Bushi?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can, yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree that the evidence or the information of (redacted) directly contradicts what you've told this Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: To what I heard, he is saying here from what he heard or from what he was told by someone else, and this is in paragraph 33. So it is not something that he has seen himself. He was told about this by someone else and this is a major difference and what is here in this paragraph has nothing to do with the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Perhaps we'll go back to the beginning of paragraph 33, please. The first sentence he says --

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, now it is okay, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The first sentence he says: "The operation of the NLA on Sunday afternoon 12 August was organised and led by Xhezair Shaqiri." Are you able to say that he learned that from someone else or from Mr. Xhezair Shaqiri directly?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can see from his statement, we have his statement before us and in this statement he says as I was told.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you able --

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: And secondly, Xhezair Shaqiri has nothing to it with 114th Brigade. He was not a member of this brigade and he was not in charge of any operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, you have said that before, Mr. Bushi, but are you able to say from this first sentence I have read to you where (redacted) got his information from about the fact that the operation was led and organised by Xhezair Shaqiri. Do you know where he got his information from, from that statement?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That I don't know. It is his problem. I don't know where he got his information from.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And when he says "When the NLA soldiers were wounded, he," that is Xhezair Shaqiri "Ordered them to withdraw to Matejce because he was informed that the Ohrid agreement was reached and the war was going to end." From this statement, Mr. Bushi, are you able to say where (redacted) got his information from?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know where he got his information from.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: What about the sentence "About 100 NLA members participated on Sunday afternoon operation in the area above Ljuboten." Do you know how he would know that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. Some say 30, some say 60, some say 100. We have seen these figures in different statements. The truth is that there were no NLA soldiers in Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Bushi, you're quite right that the figures vary somewhat between the estimate given by various witnesses. But you will agree at the least that the evidence of (redacted) directly corroborates the evidence of other witnesses including Islam Zendeli and Mr. Suat Saliu, which I have read to you earlier. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everything you read is untrue and I will ask a question, if I may. Had there been any, even a single NLA soldier in Ljuboten, why didn't they kill an NLA member, but instead they killed civilians, children and elderly people.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: We may come to that in a moment, Mr. Bushi, but for the time being do you recall that I asked about the position of Mr. Xhezair Shaqiri yesterday. Do you recall me asking you that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And in response you said basically that Mr. Shaqiri was not a member of your brigade. Do you recall saying that? And you said that today again.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you recall that I read to you a paragraph of Mr. Shaqiri's statement in which he said that in fact he was an inspector of the NLA who was active in all brigades of the NLA. Do you recall me reading that passage to you?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recall what he said. He can even say that he was the commander of the General Staff, but the truth is that he was not. And such a formation, such a position did not exist within the ranks of the NLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Isn't the truth, Mr. Bushi, that you are trying to distance yourself from Mr. Shaqiri because he is the link between yourself and the people in the village of Ljuboten. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I will ask that the witness be shown what is Rule 65 ter 1D761. It has an ERN 1D00-6818. The Macedonian version is 1D00-6824.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, this is a statement taken by the Office of the Prosecutor on the 10th of August of 2003 with Mr. Xhezair Shaqiri, aka Hoxha. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you will recall that I have shown you yesterday the first paragraph of his statement. Can you recall that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'll ask the registry to turn, please, to page 3 of that statement. That would be page 2 in the Macedonian version, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And when it appears on your screen, Mr. Bushi, I will ask you to look at paragraph 4 of that statement, please.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'll read out to you what Mr. Shaqiri told the Office of the Prosecution. "I came to the area of Ljuboten Sunday, 12 August. 114th Brigade under command of Adashi, had the villages Vistica, Nikustak, and the monastery in Matejce." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And Mr. Shaqiri goes on to say: "I was told by commander Adashi that there were massacres going on in Ljuboten and that he, half an hour before, sent some soldiers to see if they could help the villagers." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree that Mr. Shaqiri, as with the other people who talked to the Prosecution, again indicate that it is you, known as Adashi, who had sent a number of men towards Ljuboten. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't send anyone in the direction of Ljuboten. But when we discussed with Xhezair, we said that there was nothing we could do and that was it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But you agree, Mr. Bushi, don't you, that, again, the evidence of Mr. Shaqiri directly contradicts your suggest that you did not send anyone towards the village of Ljuboten. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree, Mr. Bushi, that if the presence of members of the NLA had been noticed in or directly around the village of Ljuboten on the 12th of August of 2001, that, again, would directly contradict your evidence before this Tribunal. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if the OSCE, the EUMM and the ICRC were all to say that they saw members of the NLA in or around the village of Ljuboten on the 12th of August, that, again, would directly contradict the evidence which you've given before this Tribunal. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But it was impossible to see any soldier of the NLA in Ljuboten. You should be 100 per cent sure of what I'm saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Bushi, I will perhaps ask you the question again. Specifically in or around Ljuboten do you agree that if international organisations or international observers were to say that they saw members of the NLA in or around the village of Ljuboten on the 12th of August of 2001, that would directly contradict your evidence before this Tribunal. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree but I repeat: It was impossible to see any soldier of the NLA Ljuboten or in its surroundings by any of such institutions.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I will ask the registry to please bring up what is Rule 65 ter 1D287. It has an ERN 1D00-2380. Mr. Bushi, there is no translation of this document in Macedonian or Albanian that we could find, in any case. So I will have to read it out to you.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: For the registry's assistance, I believe there is English translation of this document. It should be 1D00-2380. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, this is a document which was received from the embassy of the Federal Republic of Germany and it is dated the 16th of August of 2001, Skopje. And the subject of the document is information on Ljuboten. And I will read a number of passages to you from this document. In the first paragraph of that document, the German embassy through its military attache says this: "The varying perceptions about the same events are still leading to varying assessments and to neutral apportioning of blame. International press articles regarding the massacre, quote unquote, of Ljuboten only serve to add fuel to the fire of the two conflicting sides and the population." And then it goes on to say: "Intensive conversation have yielded the following course of events. Ljuboten has a majority population of Albanian ethnicity and one part of the town is inhabited by Macedonians. The mine incident of 10 August happened on one of the approaches to the Albanian part of town. The NLA, National Liberation Army, tried to capture the town in several hit-and-run attempts but was prevented from doing so by Macedonian security forces." It would have to be scrolled down a little bit. And, Your Honour, perhaps before I proceed and perhaps after the break I would simply indicate that in the next sentence which I am to read to the witness, there is a very serious translation mistake that has been made from the German to the English which actually reverse the sense of the sentence. We have checked the matter with CLSS which have indicated our own translation was correct, and we will request an official translation of this particular sentence. I will simply draw Your Honours' attention to the sentence which say, "There is now doubt," n-o-w, which should in fact read "There is no doubt," n-o, in the German "es gibt keinen Zweifel" and perhaps it would be an appropriate time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: We go on to 5.00 --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Perfect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: -- if that suits you, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, I apologise to you for the interruption. I will read to you the next sentence in that document. It says this: "The attack by the security forces of 12 August was led by the Macedonian part of the town against the centre of the town. There is no doubt that first three mortar attacks were aimed at the security forces. It was the Macedonian forces which then followed by using further mortars." Stopping for a moment here, Mr. Bushi, do you agree that what this document suggests is that your organisation, the so-called NLA, was in fact the one that initiated the exchange of fire with the Macedonian authorities. Do you agree that that is what the document is suggesting?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then if you can further down in this document, it says this: "It is indisputable that there were violent attacks by the Macedonian population on the Albanian population following the town's seizure by the security forces. There are no details but it is certain that one part of the Albanian population has left the town for the moment in the direction of Skopje and the Radishani suburb.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, we would seek to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a question, if I may, with respect to this. Which of the forces captured Ljuboten? It is not clear to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: You are required to answer the questions, not to put the questions. So thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Just for the record the Prosecution objects to the admission of this document for similar reasons than before, the witness has not established the reliability and the probative value of this document produced by another source.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, in response, Your Honour, I would simply indicate that this is a document that was provided to us by the Office of the Prosecution, that it actually appears on its Rule 65 ter exhibit list as 353.20 and that it was an attachment to the proposed statement of Mr. Matthiesen. As for the relevance of this document, it is again, Your Honour, obviously relevant to the issue of the presence of the NLA in the village of the fire directed by the NLA at Macedonian forces, as evidence has been given if this case and it is also directly relevant, we submit, to the credibility, or otherwise, of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As exhibit 1D224, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I will ask the registry, please, to bring up Rule 65 ter 1D320. It has an ERN of 1D00-2966. And in the Macedonian version, it is 1D00- I believe 2987. 2988.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, what I'm about to show to you is the statement of the Office of the Prosecutor which they took of Mr. Peter Matthiesen who have I showed yesterday already and who was the military attache of the German embassy at that time in Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I will kindly ask the registry to turn to page 14 of that statement. That would be 1D00-2979, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, I'm also trying to retrieve at the same time the Macedonian version for your benefit. For the time being I will read to you the paragraph in question. That would be paragraph 62 and 63 of Mr. Matthiesen's statement. Mr. Matthiesen said this to the Office of the Prosecutor: "There is no doubt that the NLA was present in the Albanian part of Ljuboten and in Nikustak. The reports talked about NLA Brigade 114, mainly consisting of reservists from the KPC" -- that is the Kosovo protection corps -- "that tried for days to attack the Macedonian part of the village in a hit-and-run strategy. As this was directly before the signing of the Ohrid Framework Agreement, there is no doubt for me that the NLA was trying to strength their position by taking control over more villages and terrain before the agreement." And then Mr. Matthiesen says this: "I wish to elaborate about my comments regarding the NLA being in the area of Ljuboten. In my professional experience it is absolutely normal that in Ljuboten, like in any other ethnic Albanian village, there were people who supported the NLA or who were members of the NLA. I had no information at any time about the presence of armed NLA soldiers inside Ljuboten. Members or supporters of the NLA, if they were present might have been armed and they might not have been armed. Some villagers of Ljuboten could have supported the NLA by logistics and/or by supplying them with information. The nearest NLA unit in the area was the 114th Brigade which was based north of Ljuboten." Mr. Bushi, do you recall during that weekend organising hit-and-run attacks in and around the village of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not true. We didn't have any strategy at all with respect to Ljuboten. The NLA was supported by the entire Albanian population, but it was a moral support.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, we'll come to the issue of the moral support in a moment. But will you agree then or let me put it another way. Are you suggesting that the evidence that I've just read to you is inaccurate?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will also refer the Trial Chamber to the evidence of, inter alia, Mr. Jurisic, Despodov and Bolton.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, do you recall being asked by the Office of the Prosecutor about the death of Mr. Muzafer Agushi who was a member of your brigade?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I apologise, Mr. Bushi. I will ask you the question once again. Do you recall being asked by the Office of the Prosecutor both at the time of your statement and yesterday during your evidence about the death of Mr. Muzafer Agushi who was a member of your brigade. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And both in your statement and yesterday in your evidence you suggested that Mr. Agushi Muzafer had died on the 11th of August in the area of Nikustak. Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You would agree, I suppose, that if the evidence was that in fact that Mr. Muzafer Agushi dated not on the 11th but the 12th and not in Nikustak but in Ljuboten, that would be --

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, sorry for -- sorry for interrupting the proceedings by the accused cannot receive interpretation in the Macedonian language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Is this problem still there? Well, is it resolved now?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is okay now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: You may proceed, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you to Mr. Apostolski for bringing that to our attention.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, I apologise. I will ask you --

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: May you please repeat the question, Mr. Mettraux?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The question was this, if the evidence was in fact that Mr. Muzafer Agushi died on the 12th of August of 2001, and not on the 11th as you had suggested, and not in Nikustak, as you had suggested but in Ljuboten, you would agree that this would directly contradict your evidence?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Muzafer Agushi was killed in Nagustak on the 11th of August, and I fully trusted my officers who reported to me this death.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, in fact if the evidence was that Mr. Agushi died on the 12th of August in or around the village of Ljuboten, it would not only contradict your evidence as to the time and circumstances of his death but it would also directly contradict your evidence about the presence of your men in or around the village. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said earlier, Muzafer Agushi passed away on the 11th of August in Nagustak village. And I had complete trust on my officers about their report --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'll come back to --

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- and nothing happened and it has got nothing to do with Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I come back to that in a minute, but before, I'll ask you, do you recall being asked about another person, Bejtullah Ademi by the Prosecution? Do you remember being asked questions about this person?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you told the Office of the Prosecution that Mr. Ademi had been injured on the 10 or the 11th of August, again in Nikustak. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, again, if the evidence was that in fact Mr. Ademi had been injured not in Nikustak and not on the 10th or the 11th but on the 12th in or around Ljuboten that would, again, directly contradict your evidence. You would agree?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I'm putting it to you that the reason why you are placing the death and injuries of Mr. Agushi and Ademi on other dates and other places is to hide the fact that they in fact were injured and killed in or around the village of Ljuboten on the 12th of August. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It is not true what you are saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Would it be a convenient time, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Yes. We will adjourn for half an hour and resume at 5.30.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, do you recall that before the break I was asking you about the circumstances of the death of Mr. Agushi and the circumstances under which Mr. Ademi had been injured. Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I'd like the registry to show Mr. Bushi what is Exhibit 1D7, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: As you can see, Mr. Bushi, this is a document prepared by the NLA, UCK and that was given to us by the Office of the Prosecution and it contains a list of members of the NLA who died during the crisis.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I'll ask the registry to show two pages in parallel, if it is feasible. That would be 1D00-1046 - thank you - and the other one would be 1D00-1052. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, I will ask you to look first at the list on the right-hand side. Can you see there is a list of names?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, can I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And can you confirm that the first column concerns the full name of the person. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree but I don't know which persons are in question here. I can see the name of Muzafer Agushi here.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If you can just focus on the top line above the name for the time being, if you can help us with the translation. Would you agree that the second column is the year of birth of the person. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the third column would the place of birth, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then you would have the year of death as the fourth column?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then the last one would the place of death. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter kindly asks the counsel to slow down for the benefit of interpretation and the transcript. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could you now, Mr. Bushi, go to the fourth name on that list. Can you see the name Muzafer Agushi?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you can look at the last column in front of his name under the place of death, can you confirm that the death is registered as Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It can be removed, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you agree, sir, that in fact Mr. Muzafer Agushi was one of the men that you had sent with other members of your brigade to Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not send anyone to Ljuboten, and the document we saw is not an official document of the NLA. I don't know what was written on that document, as a footnote, but it is not an NLA document.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree, sir, that the person who Islam Zendeli said had been killed during the operation on the 12th of August 2001 was in fact Muzafer Agushi. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what Islam Zendeli said in his statement, but my statement is pretty much clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, then, what I'm putting to you, sir, so that it is clear is that the evidence which you gave about the circumstances, the time and the place of death of Mr. Muzafer Agushi is false and so is the information which you provided about the circumstances in which Mr. Ademi incurred his injury, both time and place and circumstances. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is your opinion, and I do not agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the registry please bring up what is Exhibit P215, please. This is N000-6475-N000-6493-01 in the English. And it would be N002-7240-N002-7256-01 in the Macedonian version.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, what I'm going to show to you is, once again, the statement of Ljuboten villagers (redacted) which I have shown to you already a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I would kindly ask the registry to turn to page 8 in the English. That would be N000-6475-N000-6493-08. And in the Albanian version, that would be at page -11.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, could you please focus on paragraph 34 of the statement. And I will read out to you what (redacted) told the Office of the Prosecutor in relation to this issue. "There was one person from the 114th Brigade who got killed during fighting with Macedonian forces on Sunday in the area above Ljuboten. The name of the person is Muzafer Agushi." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree, again, that this directly contradicts the information which you have provided to this Chamber?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And he goes on to say this --

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does contradict.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: "I do not the exact of the location. Maybe also another person was wounded there, but I do not remember the name. I think his name was Bejtullah Ademi and he was from Singelic." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, can I.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, again, the information provided by (redacted) about Mr. Ademi directly contradict what you have told this Trial Chamber. Would you agree?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown Rule 65 ter 1D507. That's 1D00-4667, and in the Macedonian 1D00-4674.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, as you will see, what will appear in front of you, is once again, the statement of Mr. Suat Saliu which I have shown to you on a number of occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I would ask the registry to show Mr. Bushi page 4 in the English. That would be page 4 also in the Macedonian version, 1D00-4677.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, when it appears in front of you, I will ask you to look at paragraph 8 of this statement of Mr. Saliu.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'll read to you the second part of this paragraph. We've seen the first one already. This is what Mr. Saliu told to the Prosecution: "Our position was very vulnerable. We could not engage Macedonians by small arms fire from that position. We were trying to get closer to Ljuboten but were prevented by Macedonian direct fire. During the fighting, eight fighters of Arusha's group were wounded. And one was badly hit by mortar shrapnels all over his body and died. His name was Muzafer Agushi. One fighter lost his leg and I personally gave him first aid. His name was, last name unknown, Bejtullah, and he now lives in Singelic." Do you agree, Mr. Bushi, that the information of Mr. Saliu directly corroborates the evidence or the information given (redacted) about Mr. Muzafer Agushi and Mr. Ademi and directly contradicts the information which you have given to this Chamber. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It does contradict my statement and I will explain why. He was not there, and he is not well-informed. Bejtullah Ademi did not loose his leg. He was treated on the first day Likovo hospital, but since he could not fully be treated, he was transferred to Kosova to Pristina and I think two or three days later the doctors took the decision to amputate his leg and you can prove this what I'm telling you now with the hospital in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, the short answer to my question, sir, is that do you agree that the evidence of these two persons, (redacted) and Suat Saliu, directly contradicts the information which you have given to this Chamber about the circumstances in which Mr. Agushi and Mr. Ademi were respectively killed and injured. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree that it contradicts my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you also agree that it directly contradicts the information which you gave to this Chamber about the fact that none of your men was in the area or in the village of Ljuboten. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree, and it is true that I didn't have any of my men there.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, the -- both persons, (redacted) and Mr. Suat Saliu, have also pointed out, you will recall, that there was more than one injured person, and I think both of them mentioned that eight of your soldiers were injured. Can you recall them saying that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw that. This is what he said in his statement. But how could (redacted) know of such an information when he himself was injured and receiving treatment in Nagustak hospital? He only got this information from hearsay, from what others said.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, that's what you say, sir, but for the time being, I'm interested in the other seven or eight persons who were injured. And can I ask you this. Isn't that correct that the hospital, so to say, facilitates of your brigade were based in Nikustak. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, partly they were there but the main hospital was in Likov village.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But let's stay for a moment with the medical facilitates at Nikustak. Do you agree that the medical facilities were just next your HQ, your headquarter there, do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were nearby.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You would agree that if any of those men, any of those eight injured men had been brought back to Nikustak, you must have known about it. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would know about serious injuries, but not for light injuries. In the case of Bejtullah Ademi, which was a serious injury, I was informed timely. As for persons killed, I was, of course, informed.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But surely, Mr. Bushi, if eight of your men were injured in a combat operation which you said could only take place upon an order of yours, you would know that those mens had been brought back to your HQ to receive medical treatment. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree with that, if such a thing had happened I would have been informed.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown exhibit 2D21, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, the picture is, to say the least, not very good. Are you able to identify either of the person on the picture there?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see it. I can't see clearly who is on the picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So you are unable to identify either of these men. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only see one person here, kind of lying.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, in that case, I will ask the registry to bring up, again, please, Exhibit 215. And could with you move into private session, Your Honour, perhaps for a minute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But, Mr. Bushi, I don't think you have answered my question. My question was: Do you agree that the information contained in this picture - which can be removed - and the information provided by (redacted) about this particular picture, again, contradicts the information which you have given to this Trial Chamber about, in particular, the presence of members of your brigade in or around Ljuboten. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does contradict, and this picture is taken in Nagustak hospital. I cannot add anything else, as far as this photograph is concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But in fact your personal knowledge of what was going on in the village was much more than receiving information back from your men when they came back. In fact, the reality, Mr. Bushi, is that you were running the operation through the people on the ground. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And in fact, Mr. Bushi, you had formed contacts with your deputy or what you called your chief of operations, Mr. Nazmi Sulejmani, also known as Hoxha, and Ramadan Limaj, your chief of operations. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had contacts with all the commanders within my brigade staff, not only with these two.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, what I'm putting to you, Mr. Bushi, is slightly different. What I'm putting to you is that your evidence that Mr. Nazmi Sulejmani and Mr. Ramadan Limaj were in or around your headquarter in Nikustak on the 12th of August is false. What I'm putting to you is that Mr. Ramadan Limaj and Mr. Sulejmani, your associates, were in fact in or around the village of Ljuboten on the 12th of August and that you had phone contact with them during that period. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't agree with that. As I said, Ramadan Limaj was mobile. He could have been in Vishtice in the monastery, et cetera. While the -- Mr. Sulejmani he could have been nearby there but not at all in Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, what I'm putting to you, sir, is that not only did you know where they were and not only did you know that you had phone contacts with them, but you also gave them orders in relation to that operation on the 12th of August, 2001. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't agree with that. That is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And one of those orders which you gave to Mr. Sulejmani and Mr. Ramadan Limaj was to start firing at the Macedonian positions in and around the orthodox church in Ljuboten. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't. The standing order at that time was not to vandalize any religious facilities not only in the areas that you mentioned but anywhere where they existed.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And what I'm putting to you is that this order to fire upon the Macedonian positions around or at the edge of the village of Ljuboten was an order that you passed on from Mr. Ostreni, Gezim, who gave it to you. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not true. Had I received such an order from Gezim Ostreni, I would have carried out.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that is exactly what you did, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the reason why you gave this order to your men in the field was to trigger a reaction by the Macedonian authorities. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown Rule 65 ter 1D507. This will be 1D00-4667 in the English, and 1D00-4674 in the Macedonian. And I'd ask the registry, please --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: This is, Mr. Bushi, again the statement of your -- a member of your brigade. Mr. Suad Saliu.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I will ask the registry to go to paragraph 9 of this document. That is page 4 in the English and page 4 in the Macedonian.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, I will ask you to look at paragraph 9 of this statement, please.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I will read it out to you. It is the first sentence in that paragraph. It says this: "As Macedonian forces were about to enter the village, Hoxha," that is Mr. Sulejmani, "and Limaj ordered to open mortar fire." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then Mr. Saliu says: "They obviously discussed the situation with Bushi with whom they were in contact on mobile phone. About six or seven mortar rounds were fired. Our mortars targeted the army positions. I think that fire rounds missed the target while two hit the army positions." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I apologise, I identified Hoxha as Mr. Sulejmani. In fact, Hoxha is Xhezair Shaqiri. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Shaqiri, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, in fact, Mr. Bushi, two of the men who you claimed were in or around your headquarter on the 12th of August of 2001 were in or around Ljuboten firing mortars at the army position. Isn't it the case?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that is not the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But that is what this document is saying. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is Suat's statement. He is saying that this was the case. I'm saying that that is not the case. In my opinion, it is far from the truth. I had personal contacts with Ramadan Limaj and with the other commanders. We had Motorolas and we also had mobile phones, but it was impossible to use the mobile phones in such situations.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But if Mr. Suat Saliu is right and you are wrong, the information which you provided to this Chamber about, the entirety of what you told this Chamber in fact, would be wrong and false. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think the question is a bit broad about the entirety of what this witness has told the Chamber. I think that [indiscernible] --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm happy to rephrase, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, would you agree that if Mr. Suat Saliu is correct about this matter, this paragraph I've just read to you, the entire evidence which you gave to this Chamber in relation to what you claim was happening in or around of Ljuboten during the weekend 10 to 12 August of 2001 would be wrong and false. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you recall that Mr. Suat Saliu in his statement mentions that in fact your men, the members of the 114th Brigade, sent about six or seven mortar rounds. Do you recall me reading that from his statement?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recall, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you will recall that this is also a matter that (redacted) had mentioned in his statement. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
