utterances.text: It is -- it is his statement or their statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But the truth is, Mr. Bushi, is that that is what happened, isn't it, you gave an order to your subordinate to start firing at the army position just outside of the village of Ljuboten. Is that the truth, Mr. Bushi?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The truth is that this never happened, and I never gave such an order.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown Exhibit 1D23.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, there is no Macedonian or Albanian translation of this document, so I will read it out to you. This is a document that we received from the Office of the Prosecutor and which originates in the OSCE organisation. The document is a spot report and it is dated Skopje, 14th August of 2001. I would like to read to you a passage of that document which is towards the end or the bottom of the first page, please. The OSCE said the following from their observations: "It now seems clear that the ethnic Albanian armed group mortar fire brought to bear on to the ethnic Macedonian part of the village originally sparked the fighting and at least a covert presence of ethnic Albanian armed group did in fact exist in the village." Do you agree, Mr. Bushi, that this again would directly contradict your evidence about the presence or otherwise of members of the NLA in or around the village of Ljuboten on the 12th of August. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would agree with that. But I want to repeat: That there were no soldiers of the NLA in or around Ljuboten. Had there been such a presence, things would have been different.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown Exhibit 1D162. This is ERN 1D00-5420, and in the Macedonian translation N005-7446.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, this is a document which originates from the Ministry of Interior of the Republic of Macedonia. And it comes from the administration for security and counter-intelligence. It concerns the assessment of the security situation regarding the actions of the so-called ONA NLA in the Skopje crisis region. And it is from August of 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I will ask the registry to go to page 6 of that document in the English. That would be 1D00-5426. And I believe it would be page five of the Macedonian. That would be N005-7451.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, I will ask you if you can locate in --

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but it is not clear in the Macedonian. The text is illegible.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: With the assistance of the usher, I could give Mr. Bushi a paper copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, are you able to identify a subheading saying "Ljuboten." Can you see that in your version?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'll read it out you what this document contains, what information it contains. It says this: "Operational information indicated that during the month of July and August" --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: On the screen it should be the previous page. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It says: "Operational information indicated that during the month of July and August many terrorist groups from General Jankovic through Blace village arrived and joined to NLA of Ljuboten village. The terrorist group led by Xhavid Asani and Nazmi Sulejmani transferred to Kumanovo, Lipkovo region when they had withdrawn from Aracinovo village. Then, at the end of July, they shifted from this region. They arrived to Skopska Crna Gora region and there preparatory activities were undertaken in order to extend armed action and execution of terrorist actions against the members and objects of MOI and army."

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if the English version could be turned to the next page, please. And in the Macedonian as well, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It goes on to say this: "Ljuboten village was appointed as their (the terrorists) main logistic base. Acquisition and storage of weapons, mobilisations of new volunteers. The road that reads towards Basinec village was mined by the terrorists in several places." "On 10 August 2001 at 0800 hours on the so-called location Ljubotenski Bacila, on the forest road between villages Ljubanci and Ljuboten, Skopje region, army vehicle run over two pressure-type mines placed there on the road by Albanian terrorists. Seven army members lost their lives, and nine soldiers were more or less seriously wounded in this explosion. Immediately after the explosion, terrorists opened fire from infantry weapons against the member of the army. NLA members got logistics support from the local population engaged in aim to provide information. Actually, local residents followed movement and arriving of security forces troops in that region." Can you follow, Mr. Bushi?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then it goes to say that: "On 12 August 2001 terrorists station in Mojance and Orlance villages opened fires with mortar grenades toward the armies, the arms and security forces check-points, Kruska and Nikustak. They fired seven grenades and three of these landed in the village of Branace [phoen] village whereas other four landed in the village -- in the vicinity of village." Is that also correct that you were also active on the front in Mojance and Orlance villages on that day, Mr. Bushi?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already said that we had the observation points in these two villages, but we opened fire from Vishtice on the 10th, 11th and 12th from Mojance and Orlance, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, let's go then to Rule 65 ter --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, this would be Rule 65 ter 1D187. We believe it has been admitted as Exhibit 1D224.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, I'm going to show again a document I showed a moment ago when I indicated that this was a document or information obtained and prepared by the embassy of the Federal Republic of Germany by its military attache.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The English version I believe would be 1D00-2380. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, I'll read a passage which I believe I have read to you a moment ago in this report. It says this: "The attack by the security forces of 12 August was led by the Macedonian part of the town against the centre of the town." And then the report goes on to say this: "There is no doubt that first three mortar attacks were aimed at the security forces. It was the Macedonian forces which then followed by using further mortars." Do you agree, Mr. Bushi, that this document, as with the evidence of (redacted) and Mr. Saliu and the other documents and persons that I mentioned earlier, again confirm that on the 12th of August, the original fire had been coming from your positions and that it is in reaction to this fire that the Macedonian forces fired back. Do you agree that's what the document suggests?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document says completely the opposite of what I'm saying and stating here.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, we'll also draw the Chamber's attention to the evidence Mr. Bolton, Despodov, and Jurisic.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, isn't the truth that the reason why you shelled or you ordered the shelling of the position of the Macedonian forces in or around the village of Ljuboten on the 12th of August of 2001 was to try to lure the Macedonian forces into an incident, an overreaction with a view to use it as a propaganda tool. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, tell me, please, what kind of propaganda you mean. And we didn't need to do that. We didn't -- it was not in our interest to have Ljuboten become a battlefield. And I want to repeat that the day that the Macedonian forces, police forces entered Ljuboten in addition to killing children and elderly people, they didn't find -- after raiding the houses they didn't find a single piece of weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Isn't that the truth, Mr. Bushi, that when you ordered that the village of Ljuboten be shelled or the outskirts of the Ljuboten village be shelled, in particular the positions of the army, around the village, did you so in complete disregard for the well-being of the villagers of Ljuboten. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The correct version is that we didn't shell Ljuboten. We had no reason to do that, because we knew that the civilian population was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown Rule 65 ter 1D712, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, this is again a document that has no Macedonian or Albanian translation and I apologise for it. I will read from it. This is a report or a --

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is okay, but I kindly ask you to read slowly, if you can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I will do that. I will simply indicate to you that the documents come from the Balkan human rights organisation which is associated to the Helsinki committee. It's a human rights organisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I would like the registry to turn to page 3 of that document. That would be 1D00-6272. And there is a subtitle which reads: "Rebels are causing civilian casualties," and I would like to read that passage to you. It says this: "A senior NATO official claimed that rebels were trying to lure the Macedonian army into causing civilian casualties that they could then exploit for propaganda purposes." Then there's a quote. It says: "Let's face it, said the senior western European NATO officers, KLA saw what the results were when the Serbs killed 45 Kosovars at Racak and they are thinking of the propaganda value of something like that being made to happen in Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Racak.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it goes on to say: "Other NATO officials and Macedonian defence sources fear that the thousands of civilians trapped against their will in villages under constant bombardment north of Kumanovo just ten miles from the Kosovo border are being held by the NLA rebels partly as human shields and partly because the Macedonian forces would be almost certain to kill civilians if they launch a ground assault." Can you see that? Mr. Bushi, that's exactly what you did in Ljuboten, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that. But whoever has written that has done an absurd thing. In Racak of course a massacre was committed and in Ljuboten too, and all the world knows, not only Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: What I'm putting to is slightly different, Mr. Bushi. I'm putting to you that your order to start firing mortars at army position just outside of the village of Ljuboten on the 12th of August was intended to provoke a reaction by the forces with a view to use the incident for propaganda purposes. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't. It is not true. We didn't need such a propaganda, because we had already won the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps you can help me there. Isn't that correct that recently, for the sixth anniversary of the incident in Ljuboten, the key-note speakers in Ljuboten for the unveilment of the monuments to the victims were Mr. Ali Ahmeti, the leader of your organisation, and Commander Lisi, your acquaintance, Baki Halimi. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was present there too, on the sixth anniversary. We were represented as a political party. Actually all of the political parties were invited. Baki Halimi, Ali Ahmeti and others took the floor and they referred to the massacre committed by the Macedonian police forces in the Ljuboten village and nothing more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree, sir, with the proposition that I've put to you beforehand that in fact that's what you did by shelling the army position; you tried to lure the Macedonian forces into the village to create an incident. Do you recall -- do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't do that. We had no reason to do that. If we wanted to enter Ljuboten and concentrate there, we would have done that earlier, not on the days mentioned, 10, 11, 12.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree that the order which you passed on to your subordinates to open fire on the village of Ljuboten had been given to you by your superior Gezim Ostreni. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not. Neither Gezim Ostreni, Nazim Bushi or others gave any orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, do you recall that you indicated that you had a number of telephone conversations during this weekend with Mr. Ostreni. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall perhaps that at the time the newspaper in Macedonia published the transcript of what appeared to be the records of telephone conversations, including between yourself and Mr. Ostreni. Do you have a memory of that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I read that newspaper.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown what is Rule 65 ter 1D808, please. This is 1D00-7149. And the Macedonian translation of this document would be 1D00-7148.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise the article in question?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The article records a number of communications between various people, including yourself, and I will draw your attention to a number of those. It says that "At 8.20 Fazli Veliu told Gezim Ostreni that Ljuboten village was being shelled with all weapons available. Ostreni repeated to Valiu that the villagers should stay in the cellars and that ONA members should come out and return fire." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't but I can hear through the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, with the assistance of the usher, I can again give a copy of the article to Mr. Bushi.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It then says, Mr. Bushi, that "At 8.29 yourself, Nazim Bushi, called Halimi Bakim, Commander Lisi from Ljuboten village. Baki told Bushi that Macedonian security forces had been attacking since 800 hours because they were 'inside' in a cellar. Nazim Bushi told him that he would consult Kemal and Reshat about it. Nazim Bushi asked if anybody had been injured but Baki said he was not able to tell because he was 'inside.'" At 8.31, there's a record which says that "Nazim Bushi talked about unit in Ljuboten village to an unidentified person. That person instructed Nazim Bushi to approach to within 300 to 400 metres from the Macedonian security forces and to 'whip all of them out.'" . At 8.37, there's an unidentified person who told Nazim Bushi to form groups in order to move closer to the Macedonian security forces and attack the place where they kept ammunition. This person suggested that Bushi engage persons who know what to do, mentioning Xhavid Hasani. Then at 8.46, "Nazim Bushi informed Commander Lisi from Ljuboten that he had dispatched two units of which one was a special unit and they would be placed under his command. Commander Lisi asked Bushi to demonstrate seriousness." Just stopping for a moment there, you would agree, sir, that these two units which he is talking about would be Teli's unit and Arusha's unit which were mentioned by other people and that I have read to you earlier. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: At 9.52 hours there's a record which says that "Nazim Bushi called Commander Lisi in Ljuboten village, who informed him that was still in the cellar. Bushi informed him that the two units were ready." Then at 10.54 there's a record which says "Gezim Ostreni asked Nazim Bushi about how the work was going. Bushi told him that he had moved the units closer and that he was waiting for information in order to make a decision. Gezim Ostreni told Nazim Bushi that he should have a good decision for any situation and to kill the members of Macedonian security forces if he could. Take the artillery, direct it on Skopje and burn it down. Nazim Bushi told Ostreni that he was at position 120, near Skopje, from which he could fire directly at the city and the refinery. Then Gezim Ostreni suggested Nazim Bushi carry out a counterstrike against Macedonian security forces, that is to respond with a battery against a battery and inform him of that." Mr. Bushi, do you agree that's exactly what did you on that day?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't. It is it not true that did I what you are putting to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That's exactly what Mr. Suat Saliu and (redacted) have said, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They may say what they want.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: At 10.57 hours "Nazim Bushi called Talje [phoen] and asked him to take an 82-millimetre mortar with shells and to wait for an order to strike against the requested targets and then leave down the road where he would be unnoticed." 1333 hours "An unidentified person informed Nazim Bushi that the Macedonian security forces had entered Ljuboten. Nazim Bushi told him that they were attacking Ljubanci in reply." At 1347, "Hasan, a member of the staff of the 114th Brigade, asked Nazim Bushi about the latest developments. Nazim Bushi told him that they had started down there from the other side. Hasan replied that he heard the same from Commander Sokoli and asked Nazim Bushi to issue an order to activate fighters because the civilians were in poor state. Nazim Bushi told him that they had started and that they were not going to stop." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then there's a number of other markings. At 1348, there's Nazim Bushi asked commander Dani from Suva Reka, Kosovo to hit there with the 82 as hard as they could, to spare nothing. Commander Dani accepted the request. Do you know who Commander Dani is?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ramadan Limaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: "Nazim Bushi asked Daut Haradinaj, Commander Mala and Sami Ukshini, Commander Sokoli, to take more 82s up there. They replied that they had done it and they should send somebody to get them. At 1353, someone from Ljuboten called Nazim Bushi and informed him that the Macedonian security forces had reached the mosque in Ljuboten. Nazim Bushi replied that the forces were entering the villages but that they should not let the Macedonian forces enter and should respond with everything they had." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then there's another record at 1833 and it closes with you giving an order not to do anything, at 1833. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you know, you have indicated at that time that the Macedonian authorities were listening to your conversations, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember indicating that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, you indicated on at least two occasions that the reason for using codes and code-names was to protect you from intercepts or intercepted conversation by the authorities. Do you recall telling me that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can the witness please be shown Exhibit 1D160, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, as you can see from the cover page of this document, this is, again, information that comes from the UBK, the administration for security and counter-intelligence of the Ministry of Interior, and the document is dated the 14th of August of 2001 and concerns an assessment of the high level of the violated security situation in Ljuboten village and the surroundings. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I would like to draw your attention to some of the information which is contained in this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If the registry could please turn to page 3 of that document in the English. And I believe that would be page 2 in the Macedonian.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can you find a paragraph which starts with the word: "In the time before and during the conflicts." Can you find that passage?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is this the third paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It should start with the words: "In the time before and during the conflicts with the Macedonian forces in Ljuboten village." Can you see that? This is the third paragraph in the English.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: What about the Macedonian one? Is it also the third? Yes. I can see it is the third in the English version, but can you show it to me in the Macedonian version?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It would at page 3, 1D00-5397. And this would be the third paragraph on that page. Can you see the sentence that I read to you?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, now I can. It is in the third paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'll read it out for you Mr. Bushi. It says this: "In the time before and during the conflicts with the Macedonian security forces in Ljuboten village, Sali Mamer, member of the so-called NLA was present there together with about 30 fighters of the so-called NLA." Do you know Sali Mamer?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I see him, I might, but I don't recall this name.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The document goes on to say that: "On 12 August 2001 with regards to the situation in Ljuboten village, Gezim Ostreni informed Fazli Veliu that the villagers should stay in the basements and NLA members should go out and respond to the Macedonian security forces." And the next paragraph it says this: "Later on, a member of the so-called NLA uttered interest on the ongoing situation. He addressed an issue to Nazim Bushi, the commander Adashi, asking whether there are conditions to act against the Macedonian security forces. Nazim Bushi informed him that they can operate in villages Brodec, and Ljuboten and that in order to start action, he can deploy troops of a special unit and one more unit in only an hour and half. "At the same time," it goes on to say, "Nazim Bushi gave instructions to a member of the so-called NLA that groups should be formed and should move closer to the Macedonian security forces and attack them at the place when the Macedonian forces take over and ammunition. Also, Nazim Bushi passed information to the Commander Lisi in Ljuboten village. In order to help him, he is sending a special unit from Kumanovo, Lipkovo region and a unit of the Commander Teli. On the other hand, Nazim Bushi got information from Gezim Ostreni to undertake the counterattack against the Macedonian security forces actually to respond with a battery to a battery and then, accordingly, to provide accurate information back to Gezim Ostreni." Do you agree, Mr. Bushi, that this information appears to be identical to the information which was later published in an article which I have read to you earlier?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a similarity.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that would suggest that the information went from the UBK to the newspaper in question. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could be. As I said earlier, all the documents dating back from 14th February 2001 up to 26th of September, 2001 are not reliable because the authorities could have written whatever they wanted on them.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, let's look at the next paragraph. It says that "Zejadin Tusi, Tusi informed Fazli Veliu that the soldiers of the so-called NLA are present in Ljuboten village and are acting without any comment." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you know who Zejadin Tusi is?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it is the Zejadin Tusi that I have on mind, he was the deputy chief Chief of Staff --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the name of the organisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, a part of your answer has been left out of the transcript. The interpreter could not hear the end. Could you repeat the answer?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zejadin Tusi, currently retired. He is a pensioner. But he used to be the deputy general of the General Staff of the Macedonian army at that time, and that's why it is not clear to me why he would inform Fazliu. He was not an NLA general.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that Mr. Tusi in fact later became a member of the NLA?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He would have never become an NLA soldier. Never.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact, Mr. Bushi, that he was or wasn't, or are you giving your opinion?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He wasn't a member of the NLA. This is what I'm saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, let's turn to the next page of that document, the same document you have in front of you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: This would be page 4 in the English. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'll ask to you look at the next paragraph. It says: "In that context Nazim Bushi asked of the commander Dani from Kosovo to attack there in Ljuboten village with both units as much as they can and to attack fiercely without exemption. Sometime later the Commander Dani asked for Nazim Bushi to pull out the technique, quote unquote, ahead of all because he has four wounded soldiers of Nazmi Sulejmani, the Commander Arusha." Do you agree, sir, first that this information in part is similar to that which was published in the newspaper that I read out to you earlier?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is similar.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you agree that consistent with the evidence of (redacted) and Mr. Saliu again, it refers to a number of wounded soldiers of Nazmi Sulejmani, Commander Arusha from your brigade. Do you agree that's what it refers to?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: These statements do corroborate but they are not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, I'd like to turn to a different subject now. You've been asked a number of questions by the Office of the Prosecutor, both at the time of giving your statement, and yesterday in your examination-in-chief about the goals and purposes of your organisation, the NLA. Do you recall being asked those questions?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, some of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you told this Chamber that the reason or the raison d'etre behind your organisation was in fact to promote the human rights of the Albanian minority in Macedonia who you say were discriminated in public and official positions. Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you also said yesterday and again in response to one of my question today that you believed your group to have the support or morale support, I think you said today of the Albanian minority in Macedonia whose interests you claim to have been supported at the time. Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, what I'm putting to you, Mr. Bushi, is that in fact your organisation had no or little support in the Albanian community and your organisation was perceived by that community as a threat to their interests and to inter-ethnic relations. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown Rule 65 ter 1D822.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, this is, again, a document which comes from the OSCE, the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe, and there is no available Macedonian or Albanian version. But I will read out the relevant passages to you. This is a special report from the OSCE --

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, if you could read more slowly, because there is no Macedonian version, so I want to be clear on what you're reading.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I will certainly read as slowly as I can, Mr. Bushi. This is a special report dated --

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: -- the 21st of March of 2001 and it comes from the Skopje office of the OSCE. And this document refers in particular, Mr. Bushi, to a visit by Javier Solanas who at the time was the, let's say foreign polici supremo of the European Union, and I will read that to you a passage from that document which summarize one particular aspect of this visit. It says this: "A considerable achievement of Solanas's visit considering the uncertainty of the Albanian political parties' positions on the issue has been the formal signing by all the Albanian parties represented in parliament of a strong declaration against the 'groups who have taken up arms on the territory of our state' and in favour of more intensive dialogue when 'calm' has been restored." And then the document says that there is an attachment which is a copy of the declaration in question from the Albanian parties --

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me for a moment. If you could give me a blank paper, I would like to make some notes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could Mr. Bushi be assisted.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you. [Interpretation] You can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The document from the OSCE then attached the declaration in question from all the Albanian political parties that were represented in the parliament of the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that would be on the second page of that document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I will read it out to you slowly Mr. Bushi. It says this: "We, the leaders of the Albanian political parties, represented in the parliament of the Republic of Macedonia, stand united for peace. "We call on the groups which have taken up arms on the territory of our state to lay down their arms and return to their homes peacefully. We condemn the use of force in pursuit of political objectives. This can have no place in a democratic state. It makes political dialogue impossible. It blocks the road to Europe, which we, both as citizens of the Republic of Macedonia and as Albanians, have chosen. It could lead to tragedy for us as Macedonian citizens, and for the whole region. "We believe that when calm has been restored it will be possible to have a renewed and more productive dialogue between all political factors in the Republic of Macedonia. We call on the government to speed up those reforms affecting inter-ethnic relations on which it has already decided, and we call on the European Union to help in their implementation. "Important issues remain open. But we refuse to believe that we, the citizens of this country, Macedonians and Albanians, are condemned to choose between solutions which leave one group dissatisfied or another group feeling threatened. If old ideas have not produced solutions which are acceptable to all, then we must find new ones. But this cannot be done until there is a relaxed atmosphere." Did you know of that declaration, Mr. Bushi?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some, from what I saw now. But I would like to give a lengthier comment about this declaration, if you allow me so, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, for the time being I will ask you this. Isn't that the case, Mr. Bushi, that those Albanian political representatives who had been elected by the Albanian community and/or by others opposed your movement. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: What is correct is only Memed Tachi and his personal statements were against this, not all the Albanian nation. Only one or two members of parliament were against.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, isn't that the case, sir, that this was document was signed as the OSCE made clear by all Albanian political parties represented in the parliament of the Republic of Macedonia. Isn't that what it says?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, there are two political parties, Albanian parties in Macedonia that represent the Albanian nation. It is the party for democratic prosperity and the democratic party of the Albanians. Until then, there was the government coalition VRMO-DPMNE.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: We will come to the political situation in the country at that time but would agree that --

utterances.speaker: MS. REGUE
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. Mettraux has read a very lengthy document and I believe that the witness, he has a right to have the chance to comment on these issues and he has been stopped several times already.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: I'm looking at the hour, Ms. Regue. Mr. Mettraux, maybe this is something that we can take up --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I think I can finish the document, if Your Honour allows me to go to 7.00, I think I can at least finish the document before the end of the day, if that is acceptable to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Okay. That is fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi --

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour, really regarding what the counsel said, there is a need for me to give you a lengthy comment. I want to convince everybody here why the situation was like I described it earlier, why the Albanians were discriminated. This cannot be summed up in one word. It has to be summarized. Everything that brought up to 2001.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: I understand that, Mr. Bushi, but will you first answer the questions of counsel and then we may come back to there at a later stage. But first answer the questions, please. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, would you agree that the political parties which are represented in parliament are those for which the people have voted, they decided that this would be the political parties which best represent their interests and they vote for that particular political outfit. Do you agree that is how democracy works?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can deny what you're saying, but listen for a moment. The Albanian parties, they tried their best to articulate the demands of Albanian nation but the Macedonian political class was the one that imposed the 2001 war, because they turned down all the requests.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Bushi, we'll come to that, but could you please answer my question. Do you agree that this is how democracy functions, there are political parties which represent particular interests and people vote for them, and if they get enough votes they make it to parliament. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree this is how it should function, but the representation in institutions is a different issue, sir. We're not talking about representation in the assembly and parliament.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, we will come to the representation in other places, but let's stick with this issue in the particular moment. Do you agree that in the Republic of Macedonia as in other democracies, there are political parties for which people vote and if they get enough vote, they get into parliament and in the case of the Republic of Macedonia there were at least two Albanian political parties plus a number of independent Albanian politicians that were elected to that parliament. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will stick to the 7.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mettraux. I am afraid, sir, you will have to come back on Friday. We're not sitting tomorrow, so the next hearing will be on Friday morning at 9.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
